title: a rebuilt branch commits under the real hooks, and the hooks keep only the main-branch rules
acceptance: T-067 shipped a rebuild that never works on a real checkout. fm-worker.sh rebuilds a branch on a detached HEAD, and the repository's own pre-commit hook (fm-guard) refuses every commit on a detached HEAD. On 2026-09-24 the first three real rebuilds (T-059, T-048, T-089) all ended with 'fm-guard: detached HEAD - refusing to commit' and nothing published. The tests passed only because their fixtures install no hooks. Its own entry must be committed into design/tasks.json and its row added to design/design.md's task table on this task's branch.

fm-worker.sh makes the rebuilt commit with git commit-tree from the staged tree, parented on the fetched base, after its own marker and unresolved-conflict checks. It pushes that commit with --force-with-lease against the head it fetched, and moves the local branch only after the push lands. No hook is bypassed on a protected branch, because the commit is never made on main or master.

.githooks/pre-commit keeps only the rule that no commit is made on a protected branch (main, master). The detached-HEAD refusal is removed: server-side branch protection (pull request required, ci required, strict, no force pushes, admins included) is the authority, and the local hook is an early warning. The pre-push hook is unchanged.

Evidence is this pull request's required GitHub check and the seven gates. Tests written to fail first, in fixtures that install the real hooks with bin/fm-install-hooks.sh: a rebuild of a branch that no longer rebases publishes one commit on the new base and moves the local branch; a rebuild with a leftover marker publishes nothing; a commit on main is still refused by the hook; a commit on a detached HEAD is now allowed by the hook. Each of these fails on today's code. The worker does not run the suite itself.
Stay inside this scope. If the work needs a file outside it, stop and name the file and the reason.
